transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um, I came in because I'm having a really hard time with eating. It's like, once I start, it feels like I just disappear and something else takes over. Even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I just keep going. I can't stop until I physically can't stand it anymore.
Can you tell me more about that feeling of not being in control when you're eating? Does it feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating once you start?

Yeah, it's exactly like that. It's like... I know I should stop, and I want to stop, but I just can't. It doesn't really matter what the food is, either. Once I start, it's just this overwhelming urge to keep going, and I can't control it at all.
Do these episodes happen even when you're not physically hungry, and do you feel upset or guilty afterward?

Um, I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed if I'm actually physically hungry when it starts. It's kind of a blur, so I don't really pay attention to that. 

And afterwards... I don't know if guilt is the right word. I'm not really sure how I feel, to be honest. I just know I hate that I do it.
Do you feel emotional distress or conflict specifically about the eating itself while it’s happening or right after it ends?

Um... I don't really know if I'd call it distress or conflict. While it's actually happening, I don't think I feel much of anything. My mind just kind of goes blank. And right when it ends... I don't know. Like I said, I just hate that I did it, but I don't really notice a specific emotion or conflict right in that exact moment. I just feel kind of numb, I guess.
While you're eating during these episodes, do you feel detached from yourself or like you're not fully present in your body?

I don't think so. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel detached or like I'm floating outside my body or anything like that. It's more just... like I said, my mind goes blank. I'm still there, I'm just not really thinking about anything. I don't feel disconnected from my body, just kind of zoned out.
Do you ever feel like the eating is happening automatically, like you're not making the choice to keep eating even though you want to stop?

Yeah, that's actually exactly what happens. It's like... once I start eating, it feels like I just disappear and something else takes over. Even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I just keep going. It definitely feels automatic, and I keep at it until I just can't stand it anymore.
While you're eating during these episodes, do you feel like you're not fully aware of what you're doing or that you're acting without thinking?

I don't think I'm unaware of what I'm doing. Like I was saying, I'm still there in my head, telling myself to stop. So I know exactly what's happening and what I'm eating. I'm just... not stopping. It's not like I forget what I'm doing or act without realizing it. I'm just zoned out while it happens.
While you're eating during these episodes, do you have trouble remembering what you're doing or feel like you're on autopilot, not really thinking about your actions?

No, I don't have any trouble remembering. Um, kind of like I just mentioned, I know exactly what I'm eating the whole time. The physical part... I guess that feels like autopilot since I can't seem to stop my hands, but my brain is definitely still thinking. I'm usually just thinking about how much I want to stop. So, no, I don't forget what I'm doing or lose my memory of it or anything like that.
While you're eating during these episodes, do you feel like you're not fully in control of your actions, as if your body is acting on its own without your conscious input?

I mean, I feel like we're kind of going in circles here. Like I just said, I definitely have conscious input. I'm completely aware and actively thinking in my head about wanting to stop. It's just that my body isn't listening to what I'm consciously telling it to do. So it's not acting without my input, it's just ignoring it, I guess. I'm fully conscious the whole time.

Do you ever start eating and then realize later that you don’t remember actually making the decision to begin, or do you always feel like you made the choice to start eating even if you couldn’t stop afterward?

I always know I'm making the choice to start. I don't just suddenly find myself eating without knowing how I got there. I mean, I go to the kitchen, I get the food out, I decide to take that first bite. I remember all of that clearly. It's just that once I start, that's when the stopping part becomes the issue. But the beginning? Yeah, I'm fully aware I'm deciding to eat.
During these episodes, would you say that you feel a complete loss of control over your eating, like you're unable to stop or control what you're eating once you start?

Yeah, that's exactly it. That's actually why I came in to get help. Once I take that first bite, it's like... I don't know, it feels like I disappear and something else just takes over. Even though I'm in my head telling myself to stop, my hands just keep going. I can't stop or control what I'm eating at all. I just keep going until I physically can't stand it anymore.
Do these episodes of uncontrollable eating cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life, like work, relationships, or other activities?

Yeah, it definitely does. Um, for one, I’ve stopped going to a lot of meals and hangouts with people from my dorm. I'm just scared they’ll notice how I act around food, so it's easier to just avoid it. And my studying has gotten a lot messier, too. Sometimes whole nights just get taken over by... well, planning around eating or just trying to recover afterward. So, yeah, it's definitely getting in the way of things.
Do you usually feel down, anxious, or emotionally overwhelmed before these eating episodes start?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I feel particularly down or anxious right before I start. I mean, I haven't really noticed any kind of emotional trigger like that. It just sort of happens regardless of what mood I'm in.

Have you ever been diagnosed with or experienced symptoms of anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa, such as restricting food intake, fearing weight gain, or engaging in purging behaviors like vomiting or using laxatives?

I've never been officially diagnosed with anything, since this is my first time talking to a doctor about it. But... yeah. After I eat like that, I usually end up in a bathroom in the dorm, or sometimes I'll go find a quiet floor in the library, and I make myself throw up. I just get so terrified that all that food is just sitting there and turning into weight. So, yeah, I do that to get rid of it.
After these episodes of uncontrollable eating, do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives to get rid of the food?
Um, yeah, like I just mentioned, I do make myself throw up. I haven't ever used laxatives, though. It's just the throwing up.
